page: Amazon Web Services x8g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the ARM64 architecture and managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, with a 1:1 mapping of virtual CPUs to physical cores. Cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory density is a defining attribute, offering 512 GB of total system RAM, corresponding to an expansive 16 GB per vCPU. The server does not include bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, and it features a 15 Gbps baseline network connection.

Performance benchmarks highlight exceptional throughput in memory-bound scenarios. Uncached large-block read operations reach 390.87 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 175.81 GB/sec, placing the instance in the top 10 percent of memory bandwidth tests. The configuration also achieves high-ranking marks in PassMark database operations (46,855.81), PassMark memory benchmarks (3,267.75), and Geekbench multi-core testing (21,432.0). Caching efficiency is further evidenced by a Redis benchmark rate of 66.43 million operations per second. In contrast, integer-focused and single-threaded tests, such as stress-ng single-core (1,707.09) and Geekbench single-core (1,866.0), fall squarely within median tiers, while large language model text generation remains modest.

The x8g.8xlarge yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity and memory subsystem speed rather than compute density. Because it features dedicated cores without hyperthreading, memory-bound applications benefit from predictable execution times without thread contention. The absence of local NVMe storage requires remote storage planning, which introduces I/O considerations for persistent state. This hardware profile is most suitable for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers like Redis and Memcached, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise database systems requiring substantial RAM buffers.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by the ARM64 architecture on the AWS Nitro System. Equipped with 32 dedicated physical cores running on AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors clocked at 2.8 GHz, this configuration delivers single-threaded execution without simultaneous multithreading. It features 512 GB of system memory, establishing a 16 GB per core allocation suited for large data footprints. The instance provides a 15 Gbps baseline network interface, while local instance storage is absent and must be provisioned externally. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier results in uncached memory bandwidth and database operations, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 21432.0 and strong throughput in Redis caching. However, single-core processing and LLM text generation metrics remain at moderate levels. This server type is engineered primarily for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory datastores, relational databases, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput data processing tasks.
